task: open-tennis-robots: shoulder bolts, motor and lift screws as checked joints (flagship 10 buildable item)

doc_friction.issue: Tests share the all_parts cache keyed on Feeder params, so a new test using Feeder(plate_t=5.0001) silently broke another test that patches _cores with the same key; pick a unique param value per patched build.

deviations.why: The brief asks for revenue products; took the allocated hardware flagship row anyway because its buildable item was concrete and had real defects to find, rather than re-litigating the router's pick.
deviations.result: Five of seven joints had real faults, all fixed

goal: Land the flagship's named buildable item: measure the feeder's last unchecked bolted joints against the CAD and fix what fails.
notes: Started from allocate.py's Start-here row (open-tennis-robots). Added a 'clamp' joint kind (guide.py) and drew the four shoulder bolts whole so the sweeps see them; 7 new joints (33 total). Found and fixed: crank pin nyloc with 1 mm to the motor plate (now a 6 mm shoulder into a short insert in the rod), shuttle pin shoulder 30 vs a 12 mm stack, actuator pins of the 8 mm-shoulder size that cannot pass an M6 clevis eye (now 6 mm shoulder/M5, thin nut, printed eye sleeves, 5.5 mm plate holes), the anchor bolt's tail clashing with the guard plate above ~25 deg (arc relief), the lift spacer's set-screw window cutting away the top ear's seat, lift ear M3x10 bottoming and face M3x6 with 2 mm of thread (both M3x8). Verification here: tests/test_cad.py 177 passed (8 min, scratchpad venv with build123d 0.13.0); feeder package rebuilt (collisions [], design_rules []); run_venture_tests.py open-tennis-robots ok. Shoulder-bolt thread lengths from catalogue/ISO 7379 tables found by web search (6 mm shoulder: 9.5 mm M5 thread; 5 mm shoulder: 5 mm M4 thread); eye thickness and motor thread depths are stated assumptions.
